legend: Munir and Matthew are playing a high-stakes game on an n×m%%ZSMJ0%% grid. They take turns placing rectangles of size at most k%%ZSMJ1%% on the board. It is not allowed to place rectangles that overlap with an existing rectangle on the board. The first player who is unable to place a rectangle loses.
Assuming both players play optimally, with Munir playing first, who wins?
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤103)%%ZSMJ2%%. The description of the test cases follows.
The only line of each test case contains three integers n,m,k (1≤n,m≤103,1≤n⋅m≤103,1≤k≤n⋅m)%%ZSMJ3%%.
It is guaranteed the sum of n×m%%ZSMJ4%% over all test cases does not exceed 103%%ZSMJ5%%
output: For each test case, print 'Munir' (without quotes) if Munir wins. Otherwise, print 'Matthew'.
note: In the third sample case, one way Munir can win is by playing a 3×2%%ZSMJ6%% rectangle to split the board into two halves.
